newsitem.title: CHILE: Radio contact lifts hopes for Canadian yachtsman.
newsitem.headline: Radio contact lifts hopes for Canadian yachtsman.

text.p: A Chilean military plane may have made brief radio contact with a lone Canadian yachtsman missing for more 10 days in the South Pacific, a navy spokesman said on Friday.
Search planes resumed looking on Friday, although there was no guarantee that the boat heard from was that of missing Canadian Gerry Roufs, the spokesman said.

The navy plane made contact on Thursday with a boat about 100 miles (160 km) west of the Smith Channel, near the Straits of Magellan at Chile's southern tip, but lost radio communication before the skipper could identify himself or give his position.
"There was no visual contact at all. It was just a radio contact and it was, unfortunately, very brief before it was cut off," said the spokesman by telephone from the southern city of Punta Arenas.
Roufs was part of the Vendee Globe around-the-world race. He disappeared somewhere between New Zealand, Chile and Antarctica in an area known for treacherous seas and currents.
In Paris, chief race organiser Philippe Jeantot voiced caution about the radio contact, saying there could be confusion about the name of the yacht, Group LG2.
"I would like to believe the report. It would be fabulous. But an error on the name of the boat is possible," he told French radio and television.
Two other race competitors, Frenchman Thierry Dubois and Briton Tony Bullimore, were rescued by the Australian navy after their boats capsized southwest of Australia.
